# `scenario`

A game the player can start: its worlds, who the player is and where they begin, the rules in force, its objectives, how it ends and how it is saved (13 §3).

## Fields

Besides these, a definition takes the [keys every definition carries](README.md#keys-every-definition-carries).

- `name` (string; optional): What it is called where the player chooses. Left out, its id.
- `doc` (string; optional): A line or two about it.
- `intro` (string; optional): What the introduction screen says when the game begins. Left out, no introduction is shown.
- `tags` (list of string; optional): Tags, by which the new-game screen may group scenarios.
- `worlds` (list of object [`WorldEntry`](#worldentry); optional): The realms created when the game begins: one in this build.
- `options` (list of string; optional): The settings the player is asked about before the game begins: `setting` definitions.
- `settings` (object, name → [any JSON value](../values.md#json); optional): The values settings begin with in this scenario, by key.
- `locked` (list of string; optional): The settings the player may not change in this scenario.
- `start` (object [`StartPart`](#startpart); optional): Who, where, when and what is set up.
- `rules` (list of string; optional): The rule groups in force only in this scenario: switched on when it begins, and every group another scenario names switched off.
- `objectives` (list of object [`ObjectiveDef`](#objectivedef); optional): What the player is trying to do.
- `ends` (list of object [`EndEntry`](#endentry); optional): How the game ends.
- `saving` (object [`SavingDef`](#savingdef); optional): How the game is saved, and what follows when the party is gone.
- `screens` (object, name → string; optional): Screens to use in place of the bundled ones, by role: `intro`, `summary`. Carried for the application.

<a id="worldentry"></a>
### `WorldEntry`

A world a scenario creates (13 §4.1).

- `realm` (string; **required**): The realm definition: a qualified id, or a bare name in the scenario's namespace.
- `as` (string, or `null`; optional): What rules call it. Carried; one world is built.
- `seed` ([`SeedSpec`](#seedspec); optional): How its seed is chosen. Default `ask`.

<a id="startpart"></a>
### `StartPart`

Who, where, when and what is set up (13 §4).

- `characters` (list of object [`CharacterEntry`](#characterentry); optional): The party: one character in this build.
- `at` (list of object [`PlaceEntry`](#placeentry); optional): The places the player may begin at. With more than one the player chooses.
- `time` (object [`TimeOfDay`](#timeofday), or `null`; optional): The day and time the game begins at.
- `do` ([list of effects](../values.md#effects); optional): Effects run once, after the party is placed (13 §4.4), with `self` and `taker` the first of the party.

<a id="objectivedef"></a>
### `ObjectiveDef`

One objective as a scenario or a mission writes it (13 §5.1).

- `id` (string; **required**): The objective's name, unique in its scenario or mission.
- `text` ([text](../values.md#texts); **required**): What the player is told they are trying to do: a template, read in the taker's mind context.
- `done` ([condition](../values.md#conditions), or `null`; optional): When it is done: a reactive condition (05 §7.5) that reads truth.
- `failed` ([condition](../values.md#conditions), or `null`; optional): When it has failed: as `done`. Tested first.
- `marker` (object [`MarkerDef`](#markerdef), or `null`; optional): Where it points, as the taker knows it.
- `parent` (string, or `null`; optional): The objective it is part of. One with children and no `done` of its own is done when they all are.
- `after` (list of string; optional): The objectives that must be done before this one is shown: until then it is hidden.
- `hidden` (`true` or `false`; optional): Hidden until an effect shows it (`complete_objective` shows nothing; a rule may switch it with `show_objective`).
- `expires` ([time](../units.md#time) in `s`, or `null`; optional): How long it may be active before it fails, in universal time.
- `on_done` ([list of effects](../values.md#effects); optional): What is done when it is done.
- `on_failed` ([list of effects](../values.md#effects); optional): What is done when it fails.

<a id="endentry"></a>
### `EndEntry`

How a game ends (13 §9.4).

- `if` ([condition](../values.md#conditions), or `null`; optional): A reactive condition (05 §7.5) that reads truth: the game ends when it comes to hold.
- `on` (string, or `null`; optional): An event: the game ends when one is delivered whose fields equal `filter`.
- `filter` (object, name → [any JSON value](../values.md#json); optional): The fields the event of `on` must have, each with its value.
- `as` (string; **required**): The outcome it names.

<a id="savingdef"></a>
### `SavingDef`

How a game is saved (13 §9.2, §9.3).

- `policy` (string; optional): `free`, `single`, `checkpoints` or `none`. Default `free`.
- `on_party_gone` ([`PartyGone`](#partygone); optional): What follows when the party is gone. Default `end`.

<a id="seedspec"></a>
### `SeedSpec`

How a world's seed is chosen (13 §4.1).

Written as a whole number, `random` or `ask`.

Takes:

- a string
- an integer

<a id="characterentry"></a>
### `CharacterEntry`

A character of the party at the start (13 §4.2).

- `template` (string, or `null`; optional): The template the character is made from with every choice at its default, when the player has made none of their own: a qualified id, or a bare name in the scenario's namespace.
- `create` (`true` or `false`; optional): Whether the player may make the character on the creation screen (`create`): begin from a template offered and make every choice it has. Default true.
- `pick` ([`PickEntry`](#pickentry); optional): The templates offered to make or choose the character from (`pick`): `true` for every playable template, a list of templates for those alone. With `create` false the player chooses one, ready-made, and gives it no more than a name. Left out, every playable template where `create` holds, and none where it does not: the player is given the character of `template`.
- `senses` (list of string; optional): The senses it perceives with when its templates give it none: `sense` definitions. Left out, every sense the loaded mods define.

<a id="placeentry"></a>
### `PlaceEntry`

One place the party may begin at (13 §4.3).

- `name` (string; optional): What the player is offered it as.
- `cell` (list of whole number, or `null`; optional): A cell of the realm's base grid: `[x, y]`, the highest cell of that column a walker can stand in, or `[x, y, z]`.
- `site` (object [`SiteQuery`](#sitequery), or `null`; optional): A site chosen by query: the party begins where a walker can stand in the column of its anchor.
- `role` (string, or `null`; optional): A role at the site. Carried: the world does not record where a site's marks went yet, so the anchor stands for every role.

<a id="timeofday"></a>
### `TimeOfDay`

The time of day a game begins at (13 §4.3).

- `day` (whole number, 0 or more; optional): The day, from 1.
- `at` (string; **required**): The time on the clock, `HH:MM`.

<a id="markerdef"></a>
### `MarkerDef`

Where an objective points, as the taker knows it (13 §5.1): one of three, each an expression in the taker's mind context.

- `last_known` ([expression](../values.md#expressions), or `null`; optional): An entity: the marker is where the taker last perceived it, or was told it was (15 §7.2), and none while it never has.
- `site` ([expression](../values.md#expressions), or `null`; optional): A site: the marker is the cell that stands for it, its anchor.
- `at` ([expression](../values.md#expressions), or `null`; optional): A cell.

<a id="partygone"></a>
### `PartyGone`

What follows when the party is gone (13 §9.3).

Written as `end`, `continue`, `restore`, or an object with `then`.

Takes:

- a string
- an object: object [`PartyGoneObject`](#partygoneobject)

<a id="pickentry"></a>
### `PickEntry`

The templates a scenario offers the player its character from (13 §4.2 `pick`).

Written as `true`, `false` or a list of templates.

Takes:

- a boolean
- a list: list of string

<a id="sitequery"></a>
### `SiteQuery`

How a site is chosen for a place to begin (13 §4.3).

- `def` (string, or `null`; optional): The site definition it was made from: its bare name or qualified id.
- `tag` (string, or `null`; optional): A tag it carries.
- `name` (string, or `null`; optional): Its name, as shown.

<a id="partygoneobject"></a>
### `PartyGoneObject`

`on_party_gone` written in full (13 §9.3): what follows, the ways of carrying on, the outcome of an ending and effects run first. Written as a string alone, it is `then` with the rest at their defaults.

- `then` (string; optional): What follows: `end` (an ending), `continue` (the player takes another character in the same world) or `restore` (the last checkpoint is restored; with none, the game ends with the reason).
- `by` (list of string; optional): For `continue`: the ways of carrying on tried, in order, the first that finds a character taken. `own` is another of the party still alive, `create` a new character from the scenario's character template at the place the party began. Default both, in that order.
- `as` (string, or `null`; optional): The outcome an ending names, as `ends` names one. Default `lost`.
- `do` ([list of effects](../values.md#effects); optional): Effects run once when the party is gone, before what follows, with the last of the party as `taker`.
